profile.campus: Cincinnati metro, Ohio (Flexential's Cincinnati-market data center, West Chester)
profile.reading:
Per Flexentials own individual facility page (tier-1 operator source, https://www.flexential.com/data-centers/oh/cincinnati/data-center), this facility is located at 5307 Muhlhauser Rd, West Chester, OH 45011. The operator publishes a footprint of 43,551 square feet and 3.8 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building. Published certifications and compliance attestations include PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, HIPAA, ISO 27001, SSAE 18, HITRUST.

Greater Cincinnati is a smaller Ohio data center submarket compared with the Columbus-area New Albany corridor documented elsewhere in this registry, where AEP Ohio has approved large dedicated transmission and gas-generation projects for hyperscale campuses; West Chester and the wider Cincinnati metro have drawn a mix of enterprise and colocation facilities like this one rather than gigawatt-scale hyperscale campuses. Ohio's statewide data center sales-tax exemption, in place since 2022, requires qualifying facilities to invest at least $100 million and maintain minimum payroll thresholds to receive relief on equipment and electricity purchases, a program state lawmakers have debated narrowing as the scale of hyperscale investment elsewhere in the state has grown.

Ohio's data center property tax exemption, in place since the early 2010s and starting modestly at $4.4 million in forgone revenue in 2016, has ballooned as hyperscale campuses from Meta, Google, and Amazon came online statewide; Signal Ohio reported the exemption cost $554.9 million in 2024 (roughly four times the $136 million originally forecast) and $1.57 billion in 2025 (about eleven times the forecast), plus an additional $166.8 million in lost local sales tax revenue in 2024 alone, with one Scioto County hyperscale project alone expected to cost $33 billion in forgone tax revenue over its life. Governor Mike DeWine vetoed 2026 legislation that would have ended the exemption, and House Speaker Matt Huffman said there were not enough votes to override the veto; the General Assembly instead formed a special investigative committee to examine the program's costs. Cincinnati-area electricity customers, like ratepayers statewide, are affected by AEP Ohio's transmission and generation planning as large data center load is added to the grid, a dynamic regulators and lawmakers are actively revisiting as of this reporting.

sources.title: Ohio data center tax break costs far exceed original forecasts

reading.body:
Flexential Cincinnati is a 43,551 square foot facility in West Chester, Ohio, with 3.8 MW of critical load UPS capacity. At typical enterprise datacenter density of roughly 10 kW per rack, this capacity supports approximately 380 racks, though this operator publishes no specification of IT load separate from UPS capacity, so that figure is an assumption. The facility holds certifications for PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, HIPAA, ISO 27001, SSAE 18, and HITRUST, qualifying it for regulated workloads in finance, healthcare, and payment processing.

Within Ohio, Flexential Cincinnati ranks sixth among eight facilities with published megawatt capacity. The state has 76 mapped datacenters overall, but only these eight publish power figures to the operators' spec pages. Ohio's total published capacity is 60.4 MW, making this facility responsible for 6.3 percent of that reported figure.

For AI scaling, 3.8 MW is immaterial at current training cluster scale. High-end AI training densities now run 50 to 150 kW per rack depending on accelerator type, which would reduce the effective rack count to 25 to 75 racks at peak load. This campus serves enterprise and compliance-heavy tenants, not hyperscale compute, and has published no power expansion roadmap.
